newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares in record territory in bourse trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares in record territory in bourse trade.

text.p: German shares traded in record territory in bourse trade on Monday with sentiment lifted by Friday's strong close on Wall Street above 7,000 points, firmer debt and a stable, if slightly lower, dollar against the mark.
At 1035 GMT, the DAX index stood at 3,425.50 points, up 49.30 points or 1.46 percent. This level was just shy of an all-time high of 3,427.64 points reached earlier in the session.
The DAX index was also playing catch-up with its IBIS counterpart, which stood at 3,429.42 points, up 0.33 percent, after opening at 3,416.99 points.
Among the main gainers on Monday was engineering group Deutz, which was continuing to enjoy positive sentiment after reports last week that the group would report a profit next year.
Monday was also the opening day for trade in Frankfurt's new market for technology, new media and other growth stocks, the Neue Markt, modelled on New York's Nasdaq index.

The initial public offering in shares in German mobile company Mobilcom AG, which will trade on the Neue Markt, were more than 100 times oversubscribed, its chief executive Gerhard Schmid told Reuters on Monday.
Also due for a listing on the Neue Markt on Monday was the engineering sales company Bertrandt AG.
The share market was gearing up for a rash of corporate information this week, with the three big chemical companies all due to report this week and next week.
Results for 1996 are due on Tuesday from Hoechst AG and Bayer AG, while the other member of the triumvirate of German chemical giant, BASF AG, will report its figures next week.
Shares in all three companies were strongly favoured in bourse trade.
Bayer was up 4.45 marks at 77.10 marks, BASF was up 2.06 marks at 65.70 marks and Hoechst AG was up 1.80 marks at 79.60 marks.
Henkel KGaA shares were up 1.20 marks at 100.40 marks after it reported a stronger 1996 dividend and forecast positive business developments in 1997.
